label: first input token is 3 or x (plus strong <DEL> response after u/o/a/2-initial sequences)
explanation: Fires deterministically (precision 1.0 on dev) at step 0 when the first original token is 3 or x, at a modest magnitude (about 0.09 of max for 3, about 0.02 for x). That case covers about 55% of active steps but only about 30% of activation mass. It also fires more weakly and less reliably on 3/x later in the original phase (rate about 26% for t<=4, decaying with position; the largest such values are about 0.37 of max, for x at t=3). The strongest activations (top of the range) are at the <DEL> step of short sequences (L=3-4) whose first token is u, o, a or 2; <DEL> overall carries about 29% of mass but only fires on 1.5% of delimiter steps, and it is weak or absent for long sequences. The copy phase is mostly silent (0.3x lift). It rarely fires on other letters or digits. The <DEL> component could not be captured by a simple predicate (precision <=0.25), so the recorded predicate covers only the clean t=0 component.
